title: Baseline 5km TT — DONE
prescription: Completed 27 Jul: 5.01km in 27:46 (5:33/km), avg HR 169, 90% effort. Est. max 26:40. Zones set from this.
route_note: South, flat and measured. The rolling route makes the numbers meaningless.

title: Easy + strides
prescription: Easy run at Easy pace: 6:35-6:55/km, HR under 158 (recalibrated 26 Aug 2026 off your 2024-2026 race files: threshold 182, max 200), conversational in full sentences. Uphills by effort/HR, never pace. Zones reset at the Week 8 TT. Then 6 x 20s strides on flat: build to ~90% speed, tall and relaxed, NOT sprinting. Walk 60-90s between each. Strides train the legs, the easy running trains the engine.

items: Properly easy for 8 min, building to steady over the last 2. This is most of the warm-up.
Hold a wall, swing one leg forward and back like a pendulum. Relaxed, a little bigger each rep.
The ground-sweep one: step a heel forward with the leg straight, hinge and sweep both hands down past your foot as you rock over it. Alternate legs walking forward.
A rhythmic skip driving one knee up tall each step. Light, springy, off the ground fast.
Fast little steps driving knees to hip height, tall posture, arms pumping.
Build to ~90% of top speed, tall and relaxed, NOT sprinting. Walk back between each. Do the last one 2 min before the session starts.
Genuinely easy. This is where the session gets absorbed.
Hands on wall, back leg straight, heel down, lean in until the big calf muscle pulls.
Same position, bend the back knee. Moves the stretch to the soleus, the deep calf that trail running hammers.
Grab the ankle behind you, knees together, push the hips slightly forward.

title: RACE (easy): Rainbow Beach 11km
prescription: 8:00am start, Phil Rogers Park. NOT raced — conversational effort, WALK the dunes, finish feeling like you could do it again. Highest injury-risk day of the early block. Expect 2-4 days calf soreness. POST-FLU RULE: start only if you feel 100% on the morning and resting HR is back at baseline. Cap HR at 155 the whole way, walk the dunes, treat it as a supported long run. || OFFICIAL RESULT: 1:14:37 (6:47/km on sand), 41st overall, 27th male, 1st M30-39. Run at ~70%, dunes walked, HR backed off whenever it spiked 180+. Assignment executed: finished with a full tank, back held up, week 3 volume banked. Note: 11km winner was another 15-17 junior (51:26).

title: Rolling power blocks
prescription: WEEKDAY 4am SESSION, outside, flat-to-rolling. 4 x 3 MINUTES at controlled-hard effort, with 2 min easy jog between each. Take every rise inside the block hard and hold steady on the flats - do not slow down when the ground levels out, that is the whole point. Effort target: hard but repeatable, you could speak 3-4 words and no more. Why 3-minute blocks instead of 60s hill reps: your rises top out around 30 seconds, so a 60s uphill rep does not exist on your route. Sustained blocks are the safer bet for a course with 294m of gain (organiser figure), because 3-minute efforts build climbing endurance whether the climbs turn out to be long or short. NOT VERIFIED: nobody has seen the actual gradient profile. Recce the course and this session gets rebuilt properly. Easy warm-up 10 min and cool-down 10 min either side. No descent loading here: all downhill work stays on the weekend terrain day.
opt_out: 10 min easy. Then 4 x 3 min controlled-hard over the rolling section, 2 min easy jog between. 10 min easy.
opt_tm: 10 min at 8.7 km/h, 1%. Then 4 x 3 min at 6-8% incline, 2 min walk between. 10 min easy.
hr_note: Run the blocks on effort. Expect HR to climb into Z4 (172-181) through each 3-minute block and settle in the jog. Start each new block back under 165. If it will not come down, that was your last one. || ZONES (threshold HR 182, max 200 - set 26 Aug 2026 off your 2024-2026 race files, re-tested at the Week 8 TT on 15 Sep): Z1 recovery up to 153 | Z2 aerobic 154-162 | Z3 tempo 163-171 | Z4 sub-threshold 172-181 | Z5 threshold 182-186 | Z6+ 187 and up.

title: CLIMB SESSION - Point Cartwright (the decisive climb)
prescription: SATURDAY 29 AUG, PLAN CHANGE. The trail is a 30 minute drive and that drive is not happening today, so the trail moves to Sunday and the steep hill five minutes away takes this slot. That is the right swap, not a consolation. MEASURED FROM THE COURSE KML: Beerwah is decided by ONE climb, 800m at 9.8% average starting at the 4.6km mark, which is a third of the total gain in a single hit. Your rolling route is 5-6% and you already run it Tuesday and Thursday. A long steep hill is the closest thing you have to km 6, and it beats the treadmill on footing. So this is the session for the decisive climb (it starts at the 4.6km mark and runs into km 6; his own race splits show km 6 as the slowest kilometre of the race), arriving one week early and outdoors. ||  WE DO NOT KNOW THIS HILL'S NUMBERS. Record the run. Afterwards I will pull the length and the real gradient off the file and we prescribe from measurement instead of from the word 'steep'. ||  SESSION: 10-15 min easy on the flat sections around the base. Then 3 x 3 min uphill. Effort, not pace: controlled hard, the effort you could hold for about 10 minutes, breathing heavy but not ragged. Short stride, quick cadence, eyes up, drive from the hip. If the hill runs out before 3 minutes, start lower next rep. WALK the whole way down every time, no jogging down - the descent here is recovery, not training. Roughly 3-4 min between reps. Then 10 min easy on the flat to finish. Three reps not four because this is a week early on an unmeasured hill with a hamstring that spoke up on Thursday. ||  HAMSTRING, cleared 28 Aug: reported good, so the weekend runs as written. Uphill running is quad and glute dominant, short stride, almost no eccentric hamstring load, which makes this the safe session of the weekend anyway. If it does speak up mid-session, stop the reps, jog home easy, and Sunday's trail comes off too. ||  FOURTH REP, only if you earn it: three is the number because the hill is unmeasured, not because you are fragile. If the gradient turns out to be gentler than 'steep' suggests AND rep 3 finishes with something clearly left, add a fourth. If rep 3 was the honest limit, three was right. Do not decide this before you start.
opt_out: 10-15 min easy flat. Then 3 x 3 min uphill at controlled-hard effort, WALK down between (3-4 min). Optional 4th rep only if rep 3 finished with plenty left. 10 min easy flat to finish. Record it.
opt_tm: Fallback only if the hill falls through: 10 min at 8.7 km/h at 1%. Then 3 x 3 min at 8-10% incline at 7.5-8.0 km/h, 3 min walking at 0% between. 10 min easy at 8.7 km/h.
hr_note: Do not chase a number on rep 1 - HR lags roughly 45 seconds, so rep 1 reads low even when the effort is right. By the end of reps 2 and 3 expect Z4, 172-181. Touching 186 is fine at the top of the last rep; over 186 early means you went out too hard, back the next one off. Between reps walk until you are back under 165 or until the 3 minutes is up, whichever comes first. That matches the recovery bar used on every other climb session. || ZONES (threshold HR 182, max 200 - set 26 Aug 2026 off your 2024-2026 race files, re-tested at the Week 8 TT on 15 Sep): Z1 recovery up to 153 | Z2 aerobic 154-162 | Z3 tempo 163-171 | Z4 sub-threshold 172-181 | Z5 threshold 182-186 | Z6+ 187 and up.

title: GRAVEYARD - the decisive climb
prescription: THE SESSION THE WHOLE WEEK IS BUILT AROUND.  ||  THE GRAVEYARD, MEASURED 30 Aug 2026 off your own file. It runs from 26m up to 95m. The main climb is 870m long at 7.3% for 63m of rise, and the descent off it is about 750m at around -7%, giving back roughly 50m, with a gentler runout of about 870m returning the rest. Beerwah's decisive climb is 800m at 9.8% for 78m. That is the same length, four fifths of the vertical, and a slightly gentler grade. Nothing else you can reach comes close: Point Cartwright is 17m of rise, the belt has no footing, and the graveyard is fifteen minutes away and available most weekends. This is the session for the decisive climb (it starts at the 4.6km mark and runs into km 6; his own race splits show km 6 as the slowest kilometre of the race) now.  ||  HOW IT RUNS: a loop is the climb plus the descent off it, about 2.4km and 63m. You ran two loops plus an in and an out for 5.9km on 30 Aug, which puts the in-and-out at about 1.1km and a full loop at about 2.4km. The hard part is the CLIMB ONLY. Descend controlled every time: quick feet, short stride, eyes 3-4m ahead, let gravity do it instead of braking with the quads. The descents are not recovery filler, they are 20% of Beerwah and the part of the race you have never trained.  ||  SESSION: jog in easy. Then 3 loops. Run 2 of the climbs HARD at controlled hard effort, the effort you could hold for about ten minutes, and the 1 remaining climb easy or walked. Descend every one of them controlled. Jog out easy. About 8.3km and 199m of climbing.  ||  IF YOU CANNOT GET THERE: Point Cartwright lap blocks are the substitute, or the belt if the weather is against you. Both are worse. Protect this one.
opt_out: 3 loops of the graveyard. 2 climbs hard, the rest easy, every descent controlled. Jog in and out.
opt_tm: Belt fallback only: 10 min at 8.7 km/h at 1%, then 2 x 6 min at 8-10% at 6.5-7.5 km/h, 3 min walk at 1% between, 10 min easy. It misses the descents entirely.

title: 5km Time Trial #2
prescription: 5km TIME TRIAL, FLAT, MAXIMAL. This is a race against the clock, not a workout. There are no intervals in it and there are no hills in it. You run 5km as hard as you can hold, evenly, and the number resets every zone in the plan.  ||  MARKER FOR THIS ONE: 25:15, which is 5:03/km. REVISED DOWN from 25:45 on 1 Sep after actually reading the interval data from your 27 Aug rolling power blocks: four 3-minute efforts at 4:33, 4:50, 4:39 and 4:53 per km, averaging 4:44, at a heart rate of 166 to 176 against a threshold of 182. That was not maximal, and it is the fastest sustained running in your file. Three-minute repeats sit roughly 10 to 20 seconds a kilometre faster than a 5km, so 4:51 to 5:05 is where you sit right now. The old marker was set without looking at that session.  ||  THE BANDS, so you know on the day what the number means: UNDER 24:15 (4:51/km) is ahead of schedule and we look at raising the ceiling. 24:15 to 25:15 is ON TRACK for sub-50 and nothing in the plan changes. 25:15 to 26:15 (5:15/km) means behind on sub-50 but on line for a large personal best: we add a second quality session rather than more volume. 26:15 to 27:15 means seven weeks of training produced almost nothing, and the answer is a DIAGNOSIS, not more training - under-recovery, easy runs run too hard, sleep, or a badly executed test all look identical from the outside and adding load makes three of those four worse. OVER 27:15 means we stop and find out what is wrong before another week goes by.  ||  THE PACE LADDER TO THE TROPHY, so the numbers connect: sub-50 at Beerwah, on 10.04km with 255m of climbing at night, needs a flat 5km somewhere around 21:10 to 22:10, which is 4:14 to 4:26 per kilometre. That is the number that wins a trophy. 4:30/km, or 22:30, lands you around 50:30 to 51:30 on this course: close, and probably just outside. The ladder is 5:03 here on 15 Sep, then 4:18 at the 10 Nov time trial, then race pace in January.  ||  HOW TO RUN IT: warm up 15 min easy, then the drills, then 3 strides, then 2 min at the pace you intend to hold, 3 min easy, and go. The fastest 5km is an evenly paced 5km, so do not blast the first kilometre. If anything, run km 1 two or three seconds slower than target and take it back over the last two. Cool down 10 min easy.  ||  WHERE: south, flat and measured. If you would rather race it at a Saturday parkrun that week, use the day-swap to move it there and make this Tuesday an easy run instead. Real competition is worth a few seconds.  ||  4:30am DARK-RUN KIT: headtorch on before you leave, light or reflective top, a route you already know in daylight, phone on you. Hold or wear the light high enough to pick up spiderwebs strung across the path at head height - that is what catches people out.
opt_out: 15 min easy + drills + 3 strides + 2 min at target pace, 3 min easy. Then 5km flat, maximal, evenly paced. 10 min easy to finish.
opt_tm: Second choice, the belt flatters you: 15 min warm-up. Then 5km at 1% incline, set the speed and do not touch it. 10 min easy.
hr_note: No ceiling on this one. It is maximal, so expect to finish above 187 and quite possibly to see a new max. Do not pace off heart rate here, pace off the clock and even splits: HR lags and will tell you to slow down in km 2 when you are running correctly. || ZONES (threshold HR 182, max 200 - set 26 Aug 2026 off your 2024-2026 race files, re-tested at the Week 8 TT on 15 Sep): Z1 recovery up to 153 | Z2 aerobic 154-162 | Z3 tempo 163-171 | Z4 sub-threshold 172-181 | Z5 threshold 182-186 | Z6+ 187 and up.

title: GRAVEYARD - the decisive climb
prescription: THE SESSION THE WHOLE WEEK IS BUILT AROUND.  ||  THE GRAVEYARD, MEASURED 30 Aug 2026 off your own file. It runs from 26m up to 95m. The main climb is 870m long at 7.3% for 63m of rise, and the descent off it is about 750m at around -7%, giving back roughly 50m, with a gentler runout of about 870m returning the rest. Beerwah's decisive climb is 800m at 9.8% for 78m. That is the same length, four fifths of the vertical, and a slightly gentler grade. Nothing else you can reach comes close: Point Cartwright is 17m of rise, the belt has no footing, and the graveyard is fifteen minutes away and available most weekends. This is the session for the decisive climb (it starts at the 4.6km mark and runs into km 6; his own race splits show km 6 as the slowest kilometre of the race) now.  ||  HOW IT RUNS: a loop is the climb plus the descent off it, about 2.4km and 63m. You ran two loops plus an in and an out for 5.9km on 30 Aug, which puts the in-and-out at about 1.1km and a full loop at about 2.4km. The hard part is the CLIMB ONLY. Descend controlled every time: quick feet, short stride, eyes 3-4m ahead, let gravity do it instead of braking with the quads. The descents are not recovery filler, they are 20% of Beerwah and the part of the race you have never trained.  ||  SESSION: jog in easy. Then 2 loops. Run 1 of the climbs HARD at controlled hard effort, the effort you could hold for about ten minutes, and the 1 remaining climb easy or walked. Descend every one of them controlled. Jog out easy. About 5.9km and 136m of climbing.  ||  IF YOU CANNOT GET THERE: Point Cartwright lap blocks are the substitute, or the belt if the weather is against you. Both are worse. Protect this one.
opt_out: 2 loops of the graveyard. 1 climbs hard, the rest easy, every descent controlled. Jog in and out.
opt_tm: Belt fallback only: 10 min at 8.7 km/h at 1%, then 1 x 6 min at 8-10% at 6.5-7.5 km/h, 3 min walk at 1% between, 10 min easy. It misses the descents entirely.
hr_note: Climbs: settle into Z4 (172-181) and touch Z5 (182-186) at the top of the hard ones. If you are in Z5 in the first minute you went out too hard. Descents and easy loops: let it fall, and expect it back under 165 before the next hard climb. || ZONES (threshold HR 182, max 200 - set 26 Aug 2026 off your 2024-2026 race files, re-tested at the Week 8 TT on 15 Sep): Z1 recovery up to 153 | Z2 aerobic 154-162 | Z3 tempo 163-171 | Z4 sub-threshold 172-181 | Z5 threshold 182-186 | Z6+ 187 and up.

title: GRAVEYARD - the decisive climb
prescription: THE SESSION THE WHOLE WEEK IS BUILT AROUND.  ||  THE GRAVEYARD, MEASURED 30 Aug 2026 off your own file. It runs from 26m up to 95m. The main climb is 870m long at 7.3% for 63m of rise, and the descent off it is about 750m at around -7%, giving back roughly 50m, with a gentler runout of about 870m returning the rest. Beerwah's decisive climb is 800m at 9.8% for 78m. That is the same length, four fifths of the vertical, and a slightly gentler grade. Nothing else you can reach comes close: Point Cartwright is 17m of rise, the belt has no footing, and the graveyard is fifteen minutes away and available most weekends. This is the session for the decisive climb (it starts at the 4.6km mark and runs into km 6; his own race splits show km 6 as the slowest kilometre of the race) now.  ||  HOW IT RUNS: a loop is the climb plus the descent off it, about 2.4km and 63m. You ran two loops plus an in and an out for 5.9km on 30 Aug, which puts the in-and-out at about 1.1km and a full loop at about 2.4km. The hard part is the CLIMB ONLY. Descend controlled every time: quick feet, short stride, eyes 3-4m ahead, let gravity do it instead of braking with the quads. The descents are not recovery filler, they are 20% of Beerwah and the part of the race you have never trained.  ||  SESSION: jog in easy. Then 4 loops. Run 3 of the climbs HARD at controlled hard effort, the effort you could hold for about ten minutes, and the 1 remaining climb easy or walked. Descend every one of them controlled. Jog out easy. About 10.7km and 262m of climbing.  ||  IF YOU CANNOT GET THERE: Point Cartwright lap blocks are the substitute, or the belt if the weather is against you. Both are worse. Protect this one.
opt_out: 4 loops of the graveyard. 3 climbs hard, the rest easy, every descent controlled. Jog in and out.
opt_tm: Belt fallback only: 10 min at 8.7 km/h at 1%, then 3 x 6 min at 8-10% at 6.5-7.5 km/h, 3 min walk at 1% between, 10 min easy. It misses the descents entirely.
hr_note: Climbs: settle into Z4 (172-181) and touch Z5 (182-186) at the top of the hard ones. If you are in Z5 in the first minute you went out too hard. Descents and easy loops: let it fall, and expect it back under 165 before the next hard climb. || ZONES (threshold HR 182, max 200 - set 26 Aug 2026 off your 2024-2026 race files, re-tested at the Week 8 TT on 15 Sep): Z1 recovery up to 153 | Z2 aerobic 154-162 | Z3 tempo 163-171 | Z4 sub-threshold 172-181 | Z5 threshold 182-186 | Z6+ 187 and up.

title: GRAVEYARD - the decisive climb
prescription: THE SESSION THE WHOLE WEEK IS BUILT AROUND.  ||  THE GRAVEYARD, MEASURED 30 Aug 2026 off your own file. It runs from 26m up to 95m. The main climb is 870m long at 7.3% for 63m of rise, and the descent off it is about 750m at around -7%, giving back roughly 50m, with a gentler runout of about 870m returning the rest. Beerwah's decisive climb is 800m at 9.8% for 78m. That is the same length, four fifths of the vertical, and a slightly gentler grade. Nothing else you can reach comes close: Point Cartwright is 17m of rise, the belt has no footing, and the graveyard is fifteen minutes away and available most weekends. This is the session for the decisive climb (it starts at the 4.6km mark and runs into km 6; his own race splits show km 6 as the slowest kilometre of the race) now.  ||  HOW IT RUNS: a loop is the climb plus the descent off it, about 2.4km and 63m. You ran two loops plus an in and an out for 5.9km on 30 Aug, which puts the in-and-out at about 1.1km and a full loop at about 2.4km. The hard part is the CLIMB ONLY. Descend controlled every time: quick feet, short stride, eyes 3-4m ahead, let gravity do it instead of braking with the quads. The descents are not recovery filler, they are 20% of Beerwah and the part of the race you have never trained.  ||  SESSION: jog in easy. Then 4 loops. Run 3 of the climbs HARD at controlled hard effort, the effort you could hold for about ten minutes, and the 1 remaining climb easy or walked. Descend every one of them controlled. Jog out easy. About 10.7km and 262m of climbing.  ||  IF YOU CANNOT GET THERE: Point Cartwright lap blocks are the substitute, or the belt if the weather is against you. Both are worse. Protect this one.
opt_out: 4 loops of the graveyard. 3 climbs hard, the rest easy, every descent controlled. Jog in and out.
opt_tm: Belt fallback only: 10 min at 8.7 km/h at 1%, then 3 x 6 min at 8-10% at 6.5-7.5 km/h, 3 min walk at 1% between, 10 min easy. It misses the descents entirely.
hr_note: Climbs: settle into Z4 (172-181) and touch Z5 (182-186) at the top of the hard ones. If you are in Z5 in the first minute you went out too hard. Descents and easy loops: let it fall, and expect it back under 165 before the next hard climb. || ZONES (threshold HR 182, max 200 - set 26 Aug 2026 off your 2024-2026 race files, re-tested at the Week 8 TT on 15 Sep): Z1 recovery up to 153 | Z2 aerobic 154-162 | Z3 tempo 163-171 | Z4 sub-threshold 172-181 | Z5 threshold 182-186 | Z6+ 187 and up.

title: GRAVEYARD - the decisive climb
prescription: THE SESSION THE WHOLE WEEK IS BUILT AROUND.  ||  THE GRAVEYARD, MEASURED 30 Aug 2026 off your own file. It runs from 26m up to 95m. The main climb is 870m long at 7.3% for 63m of rise, and the descent off it is about 750m at around -7%, giving back roughly 50m, with a gentler runout of about 870m returning the rest. Beerwah's decisive climb is 800m at 9.8% for 78m. That is the same length, four fifths of the vertical, and a slightly gentler grade. Nothing else you can reach comes close: Point Cartwright is 17m of rise, the belt has no footing, and the graveyard is fifteen minutes away and available most weekends. This is the session for the decisive climb (it starts at the 4.6km mark and runs into km 6; his own race splits show km 6 as the slowest kilometre of the race) now.  ||  HOW IT RUNS: a loop is the climb plus the descent off it, about 2.4km and 63m. You ran two loops plus an in and an out for 5.9km on 30 Aug, which puts the in-and-out at about 1.1km and a full loop at about 2.4km. The hard part is the CLIMB ONLY. Descend controlled every time: quick feet, short stride, eyes 3-4m ahead, let gravity do it instead of braking with the quads. The descents are not recovery filler, they are 20% of Beerwah and the part of the race you have never trained.  ||  SESSION: jog in easy. Then 3 loops. Run 2 of the climbs HARD at controlled hard effort, the effort you could hold for about ten minutes, and the 1 remaining climb easy or walked. Descend every one of them controlled. Jog out easy. About 8.3km and 199m of climbing.  ||  IF YOU CANNOT GET THERE: Point Cartwright lap blocks are the substitute, or the belt if the weather is against you. Both are worse. Protect this one.
opt_out: 3 loops of the graveyard. 2 climbs hard, the rest easy, every descent controlled. Jog in and out.
opt_tm: Belt fallback only: 10 min at 8.7 km/h at 1%, then 2 x 6 min at 8-10% at 6.5-7.5 km/h, 3 min walk at 1% between, 10 min easy. It misses the descents entirely.
hr_note: Climbs: settle into Z4 (172-181) and touch Z5 (182-186) at the top of the hard ones. If you are in Z5 in the first minute you went out too hard. Descents and easy loops: let it fall, and expect it back under 165 before the next hard climb. || ZONES (threshold HR 182, max 200 - set 26 Aug 2026 off your 2024-2026 race files, re-tested at the Week 8 TT on 15 Sep): Z1 recovery up to 153 | Z2 aerobic 154-162 | Z3 tempo 163-171 | Z4 sub-threshold 172-181 | Z5 threshold 182-186 | Z6+ 187 and up.

title: CLIMB SESSION - the decisive climb
prescription: THE OTHER WEEKEND SLOT, and the most climb-specific session you own.  ||  WHY THE BELT AND NOT THE GRAVEYARD: the graveyard's climb is 870m at 7.3%, which is five to eight minutes of unbroken climbing, so it could hold this session. What it cannot hold is a second drive. You get one trail trip a weekend and the trail day takes it, so the sustained blocks run on the belt where the gradient is guaranteed and the garage noise is fine on a weekend daytime.  ||  THE TARGET: Beerwah is decided by one climb, 800m at 9.8% from the 4.6km mark, which is five to seven minutes of continuous climbing at your pace. It is the only kilometre of that race that has not improved in two years.  ||  SESSION: warm up 10 min at 8.7 km/h at 1%. Then 3 x 6 min at 10% incline, speed 6.5-7.5 km/h, set so the effort is hard but you could hold it another minute. Between blocks: 3 min walking at 4.5 km/h with the incline DROPPED to 1%. Cool down 10 min at 1%.  ||  PINCH SET, last 5 minutes: 3 x 30s at 13-15% at 5.5 km/h, 90s walk between. That is the 225m pinch at the 2.5km mark, which nothing else in the plan trains.
opt_out: Only if you find ground that holds 6 unbroken minutes of climbing without a second drive. Otherwise this is a belt session.
opt_tm: 10 min at 8.7 km/h at 1%. Then 3 x 6 min at 10%, 6.5-7.5 km/h, 3 min walk at 1% between. Then 3 x 30s at 13-15%, 90s walk. 10 min easy.
hr_note: Blocks should settle in Z4 (172-181) and touch Z5 (182-186) by the end of each one. If you are in Z5 within the first minute the incline or speed is too high. Walk recovery until back under 165 before the next block. || ZONES (threshold HR 182, max 200 - set 26 Aug 2026 off your 2024-2026 race files, re-tested at the Week 8 TT on 15 Sep): Z1 recovery up to 153 | Z2 aerobic 154-162 | Z3 tempo 163-171 | Z4 sub-threshold 172-181 | Z5 threshold 182-186 | Z6+ 187 and up.

title: CLIMB SESSION - the decisive climb
prescription: THE OTHER WEEKEND SLOT, and the most climb-specific session you own.  ||  WHY THE BELT AND NOT THE GRAVEYARD: the graveyard's climb is 870m at 7.3%, which is five to eight minutes of unbroken climbing, so it could hold this session. What it cannot hold is a second drive. You get one trail trip a weekend and the trail day takes it, so the sustained blocks run on the belt where the gradient is guaranteed and the garage noise is fine on a weekend daytime.  ||  THE TARGET: Beerwah is decided by one climb, 800m at 9.8% from the 4.6km mark, which is five to seven minutes of continuous climbing at your pace. It is the only kilometre of that race that has not improved in two years.  ||  SESSION: warm up 10 min at 8.7 km/h at 1%. Then 4 x 6 min at 10% incline, speed 6.5-7.5 km/h, set so the effort is hard but you could hold it another minute. Between blocks: 3 min walking at 4.5 km/h with the incline DROPPED to 1%. Cool down 10 min at 1%.  ||  PINCH SET, last 5 minutes: 3 x 30s at 13-15% at 5.5 km/h, 90s walk between. That is the 225m pinch at the 2.5km mark, which nothing else in the plan trains.
opt_out: Only if you find ground that holds 6 unbroken minutes of climbing without a second drive. Otherwise this is a belt session.
opt_tm: 10 min at 8.7 km/h at 1%. Then 4 x 6 min at 10%, 6.5-7.5 km/h, 3 min walk at 1% between. Then 3 x 30s at 13-15%, 90s walk. 10 min easy.

title: TRAIL DAY - Long progressive trail (night)
prescription: RUN THIS ONE IN THE DARK, head torch on. The race starts at 7:00pm and torchlight descending is a skill nobody practises. A weekend evening works: kids down, no 4:30am problem. Start it at 7:00pm where you can, so the body clock rehearses too.  ||  TORCH SPEC, and use the same kit every time so race night is not the first time: 500+ lumen dual-beam head torch, flood for footing and spot for descents. Backup torch ON YOU, not in the car. Fresh or fully charged cells in both. Under a beam the daylight cue of eyes 3-4m ahead becomes eyes at the far edge of the flood, and that adjustment is the whole skill.  ||  ONE OF YOUR TWO WEEKEND SLOTS - take whichever day suits, the treadmill climb takes the other. This is the outdoor one: real footing, real descents, real technical ground. Measured from the course KML, 20% of Beerwah descends at -5% or steeper, and 750m of that is steeper than -10%. Descents are the point of this session: quick feet, short stride, eyes 3-4m ahead, let gravity work. This is the day the descents get trained. Nothing else in the week does that. || 16.5km on technical ground, final 20% progressive to steady.  ||  FINISH THE WAY THE RACE FINISHES: the last 5 to 8 minutes of this run go on the shallowest sustained rise you can find, at steady effort, on tired legs. Beerwah's final 950m from the 8.8km mark is a 3.3% drag to the line, and it is where a sub-50 is won or thrown away. Nothing else in the week rehearses closing at effort on a gentle uphill.
opt_out: 16.5km trail, first 80% easy, final 20% lifted to steady. Walk the steep climbs, run descents controlled.
opt_tm: Not a treadmill session. This one has to be outside on real ground.
hr_note: Under 158 for the first 80%. The final 20% lifts to Z3 (163-171) and no higher. Climbs by effort - let HR drift, walk if it will not settle. || ZONES (threshold HR 182, max 200 - set 26 Aug 2026 off your 2024-2026 race files, re-tested at the Week 8 TT on 15 Sep): Z1 recovery up to 153 | Z2 aerobic 154-162 | Z3 tempo 163-171 | Z4 sub-threshold 172-181 | Z5 threshold 182-186 | Z6+ 187 and up.

title: CLIMB SESSION - the decisive climb
prescription: THE OTHER WEEKEND SLOT, and the most climb-specific session you own.  ||  WHY THE BELT AND NOT THE GRAVEYARD: the graveyard's climb is 870m at 7.3%, which is five to eight minutes of unbroken climbing, so it could hold this session. What it cannot hold is a second drive. You get one trail trip a weekend and the trail day takes it, so the sustained blocks run on the belt where the gradient is guaranteed and the garage noise is fine on a weekend daytime.  ||  THE TARGET: Beerwah is decided by one climb, 800m at 9.8% from the 4.6km mark, which is five to seven minutes of continuous climbing at your pace. It is the only kilometre of that race that has not improved in two years.  ||  SESSION: warm up 10 min at 8.7 km/h at 1%. Then 3 x 8 min at 10% incline, speed 6.5-7.5 km/h, set so the effort is hard but you could hold it another minute. Between blocks: 3 min walking at 4.5 km/h with the incline DROPPED to 1%. Cool down 10 min at 1%.  ||  PINCH SET, last 5 minutes: 3 x 30s at 13-15% at 5.5 km/h, 90s walk between. That is the 225m pinch at the 2.5km mark, which nothing else in the plan trains.
opt_out: Only if you find ground that holds 8 unbroken minutes of climbing without a second drive. Otherwise this is a belt session.
opt_tm: 10 min at 8.7 km/h at 1%. Then 3 x 8 min at 10%, 6.5-7.5 km/h, 3 min walk at 1% between. Then 3 x 30s at 13-15%, 90s walk. 10 min easy.
hr_note: Blocks should settle in Z4 (172-181) and touch Z5 (182-186) by the end of each one. If you are in Z5 within the first minute the incline or speed is too high. Walk recovery until back under 165 before the next block. || ZONES (threshold HR 182, max 200 - set 26 Aug 2026 off your 2024-2026 race files, re-tested at the Week 8 TT on 15 Sep): Z1 recovery up to 153 | Z2 aerobic 154-162 | Z3 tempo 163-171 | Z4 sub-threshold 172-181 | Z5 threshold 182-186 | Z6+ 187 and up.

title: Joint conditioning + mobility (~30 min)
prescription: Rest day from running. This circuit is the knee/ankle/tendon insurance policy: light, controlled, never to failure. OPTIONAL FINISHER if time allows: push-ups 2 x max-2 and DB shoulder press 2 x 8 - that is the entire upper-body program now, and it is enough.

exercises.name: Wall sit
exercises.note: quad + knee-tendon isometric, builds patellar tendon capacity

exercises.name: Slow step-downs
exercises.note: off a low step, 3-second lower, knee tracking over the toes

exercises.name: Tibialis raises
exercises.note: toes-up against a wall, shin and ankle armour for descents

exercises.name: Single-leg balance
exercises.note: eyes open then closed, ankle-proprioception for night trails

exercises.name: Single-leg glute bridge
exercises.note: hips level, 2-second squeeze at the top; the glute endurance that holds your stride together late in a race

exercises.name: Copenhagen plank (short lever)
exercises.note: side plank with the top knee resting on a bench or couch, bottom leg lifts to meet it. Adductor armour - the most protective exercise in running injury research

exercises.name: Bird dog
exercises.note: hands and knees, opposite arm and leg reach out slow, no wobble through the trunk. Lower-back insurance

exercises.name: Slow heel drops
exercises.note: stand on a step edge, rise up on two feet, lower down on ONE over 3 seconds. Achilles tendon capacity for the descents

exercises.name: Couch stretch + ankle rocks
exercises.note: hip flexors + ankle dorsiflexion

title: Strength — weekly lower session
prescription: The one strength session of the week, own time slot, no run today. Covers everything: heavy lower, single-leg, calves, core. 2 ramp-up sets before the big lifts. Placed here deliberately: the hard weekend session is two days away, not one.

exercises.note: Side plank on your forearm with the TOP leg resting on a bench or chair at knee height, bottom leg hanging. Squeeze the top leg down into the bench and lift your hips. Short lever means knee on the bench, not ankle. This is the single best guard against groin strains in runners. Added 1 Sep.

title: RACE: Beerwah@Daybreak 10km
prescription: BEERWAH@DAYBREAK 10km. Same course as the goal race, measured: 10.04km and 255m of gain from the official KML (the organiser lists 294m raw).  ||  WHAT THIS IS AND IS NOT: it is a full-effort run on the exact ground, which is the most valuable fitness test you will get before January. It is NOT a dress rehearsal for race day, because it inverts everything except the course: daylight instead of torchlight, morning instead of 7pm, December instead of the end of January, cool instead of humid. The real dress rehearsal is 9 Jan at night.  ||  TARGET 50:00-51:30. GO/NO-GO: under 51:30 and you are ahead of schedule; 51:30 to 53 is on plan; 53 to 56 means the A goal needs a perfect eight weeks; over 56 and we recalibrate honestly. Read the number knowing January is hotter and darker, so the same fitness will run slower on race night.  ||  RUN IT BY THE COURSE: controlled through the 625m at -11.7% from the 1.9km mark, do not let the descent tempt you. Short pinch at 2.5km, 225m at 13%, power-hike it if running costs more than it saves. The race is decided on the 800m at 9.8% from 4.6km: get there with something left. Then the last 950m from 8.8km is a 3.3% drag to the line, so leave enough to push it.
opt_out: Race day. Full effort on the real course, in daylight.
opt_tm: Not a treadmill session.
hr_note: No ceiling. Expect Z4 to Z5 for most of it and above 187 on the climb and the finish. Pace by segment and feel, not by the watch. || ZONES (threshold HR 182, max 200): Z1 up to 153 | Z2 154-162 | Z3 163-171 | Z4 172-181 | Z5 182-186 | Z6+ 187 and up.

title: CLIMB SESSION - the decisive climb
prescription: THE OTHER WEEKEND SLOT, and the most climb-specific session you own.  ||  WHY THE BELT AND NOT THE GRAVEYARD: the graveyard's climb is 870m at 7.3%, which is five to eight minutes of unbroken climbing, so it could hold this session. What it cannot hold is a second drive. You get one trail trip a weekend and the trail day takes it, so the sustained blocks run on the belt where the gradient is guaranteed and the garage noise is fine on a weekend daytime.  ||  THE TARGET: Beerwah is decided by one climb, 800m at 9.8% from the 4.6km mark, which is five to seven minutes of continuous climbing at your pace. It is the only kilometre of that race that has not improved in two years.  ||  SESSION: warm up 10 min at 8.7 km/h at 1%. Then 3 x 10 min at 10-12% incline, speed 6.5-7.5 km/h, set so the effort is hard but you could hold it another minute. Between blocks: 3 min walking at 4.5 km/h with the incline DROPPED to 1%. Cool down 10 min at 1%.  ||  PINCH SET, last 5 minutes: 3 x 30s at 13-15% at 5.5 km/h, 90s walk between. That is the 225m pinch at the 2.5km mark, which nothing else in the plan trains.
opt_out: Only if you find ground that holds 10 unbroken minutes of climbing without a second drive. Otherwise this is a belt session.
opt_tm: 10 min at 8.7 km/h at 1%. Then 3 x 10 min at 10-12%, 6.5-7.5 km/h, 3 min walk at 1% between. Then 3 x 30s at 13-15%, 90s walk. 10 min easy.
hr_note: Blocks should settle in Z4 (172-181) and touch Z5 (182-186) by the end of each one. If you are in Z5 within the first minute the incline or speed is too high. Walk recovery until back under 165 before the next block. || ZONES (threshold HR 182, max 200 - set 26 Aug 2026 off your 2024-2026 race files, re-tested at the Week 8 TT on 15 Sep): Z1 recovery up to 153 | Z2 aerobic 154-162 | Z3 tempo 163-171 | Z4 sub-threshold 172-181 | Z5 threshold 182-186 | Z6+ 187 and up.

exercises.name: Tibialis raises
exercises.note: toes-up against a wall, shin and ankle armour for descents

exercises.name: Single-leg balance
exercises.note: eyes open then closed, ankle-proprioception for night trails

exercises.name: Single-leg glute bridge

title: TRAIL DAY - Long w/ race-effort (night)
prescription: RUN THIS ONE IN THE DARK, head torch on. The race starts at 7:00pm and torchlight descending is a skill nobody practises. A weekend evening works: kids down, no 4:30am problem. Start it at 7:00pm where you can, so the body clock rehearses too.  ||  TORCH SPEC, and use the same kit every time so race night is not the first time: 500+ lumen dual-beam head torch, flood for footing and spot for descents. Backup torch ON YOU, not in the car. Fresh or fully charged cells in both. Under a beam the daylight cue of eyes 3-4m ahead becomes eyes at the far edge of the flood, and that adjustment is the whole skill.  ||  ONE OF YOUR TWO WEEKEND SLOTS - take whichever day suits, the treadmill climb takes the other. This is the outdoor one: real footing, real descents, real technical ground. Measured from the course KML, 20% of Beerwah descends at -5% or steeper, and 750m of that is steeper than -10%. Descents are the point of this session: quick feet, short stride, eyes 3-4m ahead, let gravity work. This is the day the descents get trained. Nothing else in the week does that. || 13.5km with 2 x 10 min at race effort. Night run, head torch.  ||  FINISH THE WAY THE RACE FINISHES: the last 5 to 8 minutes of this run go on the shallowest sustained rise you can find, at steady effort, on tired legs. Beerwah's final 950m from the 8.8km mark is a 3.3% drag to the line, and it is where a sub-50 is won or thrown away. Nothing else in the week rehearses closing at effort on a gentle uphill.  ||  HEAT, and this matters more than it looks: the race is 7:00pm on a humid Queensland night at 25C or more, and almost every run in this plan happens at 4:30am, the coolest hour of the day. From here, run this session in the evening rather than the morning wherever the weekend allows, and carry fluid with electrolytes on anything over an hour. On weeks where the timing does not work, take the exposure from a 30 min hot bath at about 40C straight after the run instead - the adaptation comes from raised core temperature, not from the running.
opt_out: 13.5km trail, easy, with 2 x 10 min at race effort. Walk the steep climbs, run descents controlled.
opt_tm: Not a treadmill session. This one has to be outside on real ground.
hr_note: Easy under 158 either side of the blocks. During the race-effort blocks expect Z4 (172-181), drifting to Z5 (182-186) on the climbs. Climbs by effort, never pace. || ZONES (threshold HR 182, max 200 - set 26 Aug 2026 off your 2024-2026 race files, re-tested at the Week 8 TT on 15 Sep): Z1 recovery up to 153 | Z2 aerobic 154-162 | Z3 tempo 163-171 | Z4 sub-threshold 172-181 | Z5 threshold 182-186 | Z6+ 187 and up.

title: CLIMB SESSION - the decisive climb
prescription: THE OTHER WEEKEND SLOT, and the most climb-specific session you own.  ||  WHY THE BELT AND NOT THE GRAVEYARD: the graveyard's climb is 870m at 7.3%, which is five to eight minutes of unbroken climbing, so it could hold this session. What it cannot hold is a second drive. You get one trail trip a weekend and the trail day takes it, so the sustained blocks run on the belt where the gradient is guaranteed and the garage noise is fine on a weekend daytime.  ||  THE TARGET: Beerwah is decided by one climb, 800m at 9.8% from the 4.6km mark, which is five to seven minutes of continuous climbing at your pace. It is the only kilometre of that race that has not improved in two years.  ||  SESSION: warm up 10 min at 8.7 km/h at 1%. Then 3 x 9 min at 10-12% incline, speed 6.5-7.5 km/h, set so the effort is hard but you could hold it another minute. Between blocks: 3 min walking at 4.5 km/h with the incline DROPPED to 1%. Cool down 10 min at 1%.  ||  PINCH SET, last 5 minutes: 3 x 30s at 13-15% at 5.5 km/h, 90s walk between. That is the 225m pinch at the 2.5km mark, which nothing else in the plan trains.  ||  HEAT, and this matters more than it looks: the race is 7:00pm on a humid Queensland night at 25C or more, and almost every run in this plan happens at 4:30am, the coolest hour of the day. From here, run this session in the evening rather than the morning wherever the weekend allows, and carry fluid with electrolytes on anything over an hour. On weeks where the timing does not work, take the exposure from a 30 min hot bath at about 40C straight after the run instead - the adaptation comes from raised core temperature, not from the running.
opt_out: Only if you find ground that holds 9 unbroken minutes of climbing without a second drive. Otherwise this is a belt session.
opt_tm: 10 min at 8.7 km/h at 1%. Then 3 x 9 min at 10-12%, 6.5-7.5 km/h, 3 min walk at 1% between. Then 3 x 30s at 13-15%, 90s walk. 10 min easy.
hr_note: Blocks should settle in Z4 (172-181) and touch Z5 (182-186) by the end of each one. If you are in Z5 within the first minute the incline or speed is too high. Walk recovery until back under 165 before the next block. || ZONES (threshold HR 182, max 200 - set 26 Aug 2026 off your 2024-2026 race files, re-tested at the Week 8 TT on 15 Sep): Z1 recovery up to 153 | Z2 aerobic 154-162 | Z3 tempo 163-171 | Z4 sub-threshold 172-181 | Z5 threshold 182-186 | Z6+ 187 and up.

title: 5km Time Trial #4
prescription: 5km TIME TRIAL, FLAT, MAXIMAL. This is a race against the clock, not a workout. There are no intervals in it and there are no hills in it. You run 5km as hard as you can hold, evenly, and the number resets every zone in the plan.  ||  FINAL GO/NO-GO on the A goal. Whatever this says, we plan the race off it honestly.  ||  HOW TO RUN IT: warm up 15 min easy, then the drills, then 3 strides, then 2 min at the pace you intend to hold, 3 min easy, and go. The fastest 5km is an evenly paced 5km, so do not blast the first kilometre. If anything, run km 1 two or three seconds slower than target and take it back over the last two. Cool down 10 min easy.  ||  WHERE: south, flat and measured. If you would rather race it at a Saturday parkrun that week, use the day-swap to move it there and make this Tuesday an easy run instead. Real competition is worth a few seconds.  ||  4:30am DARK-RUN KIT: headtorch on before you leave, light or reflective top, a route you already know in daylight, phone on you. Hold or wear the light high enough to pick up spiderwebs strung across the path at head height - that is what catches people out.
opt_out: 15 min easy + drills + 3 strides + 2 min at target pace, 3 min easy. Then 5km flat, maximal, evenly paced. 10 min easy to finish.
opt_tm: Second choice, the belt flatters you: 15 min warm-up. Then 5km at 1% incline, set the speed and do not touch it. 10 min easy.
hr_note: No ceiling on this one. It is maximal, so expect to finish above 187 and quite possibly to see a new max. Do not pace off heart rate here, pace off the clock and even splits: HR lags and will tell you to slow down in km 2 when you are running correctly. || ZONES (threshold HR 182, max 200 - set 26 Aug 2026 off your 2024-2026 race files, re-tested at the Week 8 TT on 15 Sep): Z1 recovery up to 153 | Z2 aerobic 154-162 | Z3 tempo 163-171 | Z4 sub-threshold 172-181 | Z5 threshold 182-186 | Z6+ 187 and up.

title: TRAIL DAY - Long w/ race-effort (night)
prescription: RUN THIS ONE IN THE DARK, head torch on. The race starts at 7:00pm and torchlight descending is a skill nobody practises. A weekend evening works: kids down, no 4:30am problem. Start it at 7:00pm where you can, so the body clock rehearses too.  ||  TORCH SPEC, and use the same kit every time so race night is not the first time: 500+ lumen dual-beam head torch, flood for footing and spot for descents. Backup torch ON YOU, not in the car. Fresh or fully charged cells in both. This is the outdoor one: real footing, real descents, real technical ground. Measured from the course KML, 20% of Beerwah descends at -5% or steeper, and 750m of that is steeper than -10%. Descents are the point of this session: quick feet, short stride, eyes 3-4m ahead, let gravity work. This is the day the descents get trained. Nothing else in the week does that. || 16.0km with 2 x 10 min at race effort.  ||  FINISH THE WAY THE RACE FINISHES: the last 5 to 8 minutes of this run go on the shallowest sustained rise you can find, at steady effort, on tired legs. title: CLIMB SESSION - the decisive climb
prescription: THE OTHER WEEKEND SLOT, and the most climb-specific session you own.  ||  WHY THE BELT AND NOT THE GRAVEYARD: the graveyard's climb is 870m at 7.3%, which is five to eight minutes of unbroken climbing, so it could hold this session. What it cannot hold is a second drive. You get one trail trip a weekend and the trail day takes it, so the sustained blocks run on the belt where the gradient is guaranteed and the garage noise is fine on a weekend daytime.  ||  THE TARGET: Beerwah is decided by one climb, 800m at 9.8% from the 4.6km mark, which is five to seven minutes of continuous climbing at your pace. It is the only kilometre of that race that has not improved in two years.  ||  SESSION: warm up 10 min at 8.7 km/h at 1%. Then 3 x 11 min at 10-12% incline, speed 6.5-7.5 km/h, set so the effort is hard but you could hold it another minute. Between blocks: 3 min walking at 4.5 km/h with the incline DROPPED to 1%. Cool down 10 min at 1%.  ||  PINCH SET, last 5 minutes: 3 x 30s at 13-15% at 5.5 km/h, 90s walk between. That is the 225m pinch at the 2.5km mark, which nothing else in the plan trains.  ||  HEAT, and this matters more than it looks: the race is 7:00pm on a humid Queensland night at 25C or more, and almost every run in this plan happens at 4:30am, the coolest hour of the day. From here, run this session in the evening rather than the morning wherever the weekend allows, and carry fluid with electrolytes on anything over an hour. On weeks where the timing does not work, take the exposure from a 30 min hot bath at about 40C straight after the run instead - the adaptation comes from raised core temperature, not from the running.
opt_out: Only if you find ground that holds 11 unbroken minutes of climbing without a second drive. Otherwise this is a belt session.
opt_tm: 10 min at 8.7 km/h at 1%. Then 3 x 11 min at 10-12%, 6.5-7.5 km/h, 3 min walk at 1% between. Then 3 x 30s at 13-15%, 90s walk. 10 min easy.
hr_note: Blocks should settle in Z4 (172-181) and touch Z5 (182-186) by the end of each one. If you are in Z5 within the first minute the incline or speed is too high. Walk recovery until back under 165 before the next block. || ZONES (threshold HR 182, max 200 - set 26 Aug 2026 off your 2024-2026 race files, re-tested at the Week 8 TT on 15 Sep): Z1 recovery up to 153 | Z2 aerobic 154-162 | Z3 tempo 163-171 | Z4 sub-threshold 172-181 | Z5 threshold 182-186 | Z6+ 187 and up.

exercises.note: off a low step, 3-second lower, knee tracking over the toes

exercises.name: Tibialis raises
exercises.note: toes-up against a wall, shin and ankle armour for descents

exercises.name: Single-leg balance
exercises.note: eyes open then closed, ankle-proprioception for night trails

title: Joint conditioning + mobility (~30 min)
prescription: Rest day from running. This circuit is the knee/ankle/tendon insurance policy: light, controlled, never to failure. OPTIONAL FINISHER if time allows: push-ups 2 x max-2 and DB shoulder press 2 x 8 - that is the entire upper-body program now, and it is enough.

exercises.name: Slow step-downs
exercises.note: off a low step, 3-second lower, knee tracking over the toes

exercises.name: Tibialis raises
exercises.note: toes-up against a wall, shin and ankle armour for descents

exercises.name: Single-leg balance
exercises.note: eyes open then closed, ankle-proprioception for night trails

exercises.name: Single-leg glute bridge
exercises.note: hips level, 2-second squeeze at the top; the glute endurance that holds your stride together late in a race

exercises.note: hands and knees, opposite arm and leg reach out slow, no wobble through the trunk. Lower-back insurance

exercises.note: stand on a step edge, rise up on two feet, lower down on ONE over 3 seconds. Achilles tendon capacity for the descents

title: TRAIL DAY - Long run w/ race-effort blocks (night)
prescription: TAPER BEGINS. Cut to 11km: intensity stays, volume comes down. RUN THIS ONE IN THE DARK, head torch on. The race starts at 7:00pm and torchlight descending is a skill nobody practises. A weekend evening works: kids down, no 4:30am problem. Start it at 7:00pm where you can, so the body clock rehearses too.  ||  TORCH SPEC, and use the same kit every time so race night is not the first time: 500+ lumen dual-beam head torch, flood for footing and spot for descents. Backup torch ON YOU, not in the car. Fresh or fully charged cells in both. Under a beam the daylight cue of eyes 3-4m ahead becomes eyes at the far edge of the flood, and that adjustment is the whole skill.  ||  ONE OF YOUR TWO WEEKEND SLOTS - take whichever day suits, the treadmill climb takes the other. This is the outdoor one: real footing, real descents, real technical ground. Measured from the course KML, 20% of Beerwah descends at -5% or steeper, and 750m of that is steeper than -10%. Descents are the point of this session: quick feet, short stride, eyes 3-4m ahead, let gravity work. This is the day the descents get trained. Nothing else in the week does that. || 14km with 2 x 10 min at race effort on trail.  ||  FINISH THE WAY THE RACE FINISHES: the last 5 to 8 minutes of this run go on the shallowest sustained rise you can find, at steady effort, on tired legs. Beerwah's final 950m from the 8.8km mark is a 3.3% drag to the line, and it is where a sub-50 is won or thrown away. Nothing else in the week rehearses closing at effort on a gentle uphill.  ||  HEAT, and this matters more than it looks: the race is 7:00pm on a humid Queensland night at 25C or more, and almost every run in this plan happens at 4:30am, the coolest hour of the day. From here, run this session in the evening rather than the morning wherever the weekend allows, and carry fluid with electrolytes on anything over an hour. On weeks where the timing does not work, take the exposure from a 30 min hot bath at about 40C straight after the run instead - the adaptation comes from raised core temperature, not from the running.
opt_out: 14km trail, easy, with 2 x 10 min at race effort. Walk the steep climbs, run descents controlled.
opt_tm: Not a treadmill session. This one has to be outside on real ground.
hr_note: Easy under 158 either side of the blocks. During the race-effort blocks expect Z4 (172-181), drifting to Z5 (182-186) on the climbs. Climbs by effort, never pace. || ZONES (threshold HR 182, max 200 - set 26 Aug 2026 off your 2024-2026 race files, re-tested at the Week 8 TT on 15 Sep): Z1 recovery up to 153 | Z2 aerobic 154-162 | Z3 tempo 163-171 | Z4 sub-threshold 172-181 | Z5 threshold 182-186 | Z6+ 187 and up.

title: CLIMB SESSION - the decisive climb
prescription: THE OTHER WEEKEND SLOT, and the most climb-specific session you own.  ||  WHY THE BELT AND NOT THE GRAVEYARD: the graveyard's climb is 870m at 7.3%, which is five to eight minutes of unbroken climbing, so it could hold this session. What it cannot hold is a second drive. You get one trail trip a weekend and the trail day takes it, so the sustained blocks run on the belt where the gradient is guaranteed and the garage noise is fine on a weekend daytime.  ||  THE TARGET: Beerwah is decided by one climb, 800m at 9.8% from the 4.6km mark, which is five to seven minutes of continuous climbing at your pace. It is the only kilometre of that race that has not improved in two years.  ||  SESSION: warm up 10 min at 8.7 km/h at 1%. Then 2 x 10 min at 10-12% incline, speed 6.5-7.5 km/h, set so the effort is hard but you could hold it another minute. Between blocks: 3 min walking at 4.5 km/h with the incline DROPPED to 1%. Cool down 10 min at 1%.  ||  PINCH SET, last 5 minutes: 3 x 30s at 13-15% at 5.5 km/h, 90s walk between. That is the 225m pinch at the 2.5km mark, which nothing else in the plan trains.  ||  HEAT, and this matters more than it looks: the race is 7:00pm on a humid Queensland night at 25C or more, and almost every run in this plan happens at 4:30am, the coolest hour of the day. From here, run this session in the evening rather than the morning wherever the weekend allows, and carry fluid with electrolytes on anything over an hour. On weeks where the timing does not work, take the exposure from a 30 min hot bath at about 40C straight after the run instead - the adaptation comes from raised core temperature, not from the running.
opt_out: Only if you find ground that holds 10 unbroken minutes of climbing without a second drive. Otherwise this is a belt session.
opt_tm: 10 min at 8.7 km/h at 1%. Then 2 x 10 min at 10-12%, 6.5-7.5 km/h, 3 min walk at 1% between. Then 3 x 30s at 13-15%, 90s walk. 10 min easy.
hr_note: Blocks should settle in Z4 (172-181) and touch Z5 (182-186) by the end of each one. If you are in Z5 within the first minute the incline or speed is too high. Walk recovery until back under 165 before the next block. || ZONES (threshold HR 182, max 200 - set 26 Aug 2026 off your 2024-2026 race files, re-tested at the Week 8 TT on 15 Sep): Z1 recovery up to 153 | Z2 aerobic 154-162 | Z3 tempo 163-171 | Z4 sub-threshold 172-181 | Z5 threshold 182-186 | Z6+ 187 and up.

title: TRAIL DAY - Taper long run (night)
prescription: RUN THIS ONE IN THE DARK, head torch on. The race starts at 7:00pm and torchlight descending is a skill nobody practises. A weekend evening works: kids down, no 4:30am problem. Start it at 7:00pm where you can, so the body clock rehearses too.  ||  TORCH SPEC, and use the same kit every time so race night is not the first time: 500+ lumen dual-beam head torch, flood for footing and spot for descents. Backup torch ON YOU, not in the car. Fresh or fully charged cells in both. Under a beam the daylight cue of eyes 3-4m ahead becomes eyes at the far edge of the flood, and that adjustment is the whole skill.  ||  ONE OF YOUR TWO WEEKEND SLOTS - take whichever day suits, the treadmill climb takes the other. This is the outdoor one: real footing, real descents, real technical ground. Measured from the course KML, 20% of Beerwah descends at -5% or steeper, and 750m of that is steeper than -10%. Descents are the point of this session: quick feet, short stride, eyes 3-4m ahead, let gravity work. This is the day the descents get trained. Nothing else in the week does that. || 12km easy trail with 3-4 strides late.  ||  FINISH THE WAY THE RACE FINISHES: the last 5 to 8 minutes of this run go on the shallowest sustained rise you can find, at steady effort, on tired legs. Beerwah's final 950m from the 8.8km mark is a 3.3% drag to the line, and it is where a sub-50 is won or thrown away. Nothing else in the week rehearses closing at effort on a gentle uphill.  ||  HEAT, and this matters more than it looks: the race is 7:00pm on a humid Queensland night at 25C or more, and almost every run in this plan happens at 4:30am, the coolest hour of the day. From here, run this session in the evening rather than the morning wherever the weekend allows, and carry fluid with electrolytes on anything over an hour. On weeks where the timing does not work, take the exposure from a 30 min hot bath at about 40C straight after the run instead - the adaptation comes from raised core temperature, not from the running.
opt_out: 12km trail, easy throughout. Walk the steep climbs, run descents controlled.
opt_tm: Not a treadmill session. This one has to be outside on real ground.

title: CLIMB SESSION - the decisive climb
prescription: THE OTHER WEEKEND SLOT, and the most climb-specific session you own.  ||  WHY THE BELT AND NOT THE GRAVEYARD: the graveyard's climb is 870m at 7.3%, which is five to eight minutes of unbroken climbing, so it could hold this session. What it cannot hold is a second drive. You get one trail trip a weekend and the trail day takes it, so the sustained blocks run on the belt where the gradient is guaranteed and the garage noise is fine on a weekend daytime.  ||  THE TARGET: Beerwah is decided by one climb, 800m at 9.8% from the 4.6km mark, which is five to seven minutes of continuous climbing at your pace. It is the only kilometre of that race that has not improved in two years.  ||  SESSION: warm up 10 min at 8.7 km/h at 1%. Then 2 x 8 min at 10% incline, speed 6.5-7.5 km/h, set so the effort is hard but you could hold it another minute. Between blocks: 3 min walking at 4.5 km/h with the incline DROPPED to 1%. Cool down 10 min at 1%.  ||  PINCH SET, last 5 minutes: 3 x 30s at 13-15% at 5.5 km/h, 90s walk between. That is the 225m pinch at the 2.5km mark, which nothing else in the plan trains.  ||  HEAT, and this matters more than it looks: the race is 7:00pm on a humid Queensland night at 25C or more, and almost every run in this plan happens at 4:30am, the coolest hour of the day. From here, run this session in the evening rather than the morning wherever the weekend allows, and carry fluid with electrolytes on anything over an hour. On weeks where the timing does not work, take the exposure from a 30 min hot bath at about 40C straight after the run instead - the adaptation comes from raised core temperature, not from the running.

title: RACE: BEERWAH@NIGHT 10km - 7:00PM
prescription: THE ONE. Sat 30 Jan 2027, 7:00pm start, Mt Beerwah.  ||  THE COURSE, measured from the official KML: 10.04km and 255m of gain (the organiser lists 294m raw). 29% of it is flat. There is ONE climb that decides the race and it is not at the end.  ||  RACE BY SEGMENT, and know these four landmarks cold:  (1) 0 to 1.9km, settle. Seed yourself top ten into the first single track, because passing in torchlight is expensive and there is no polite way to do it.  (2) 1.9 to 2.5km, the steepest descent on the course: 625m at -11.7%. You will be fresh and it will feel free. It is not. Quick feet, short stride, no braking, eyes at the far edge of your flood beam. Wreck your quads here and you cannot climb at 4.6km.  (3) 2.5km, a short pinch, 225m at 13%. Sixty to seventy seconds. Power-hike it if running costs more than it saves.  (4) 4.6 to 5.4km, THE RACE: 800m at 9.8%, a third of the entire climb of the day in one hit. Arrive with something left. Effort, never pace. This is the kilometre that has not improved in two years and the whole build has been aimed at it.  (5) 8.8km to the line, 950m at 3.3%. A shallow drag on empty legs, and the place a sub-50 is won or thrown away. Whatever you have left goes here.  ||  LIGHT: 500+ lumen dual-beam head torch, flood for footing and spot for descents. Backup torch ON YOU, not in the car. Fresh or fully charged cells in both, checked at 6pm. Same torch you rehearsed with on 9 Jan, no new gear.  ||  HEAT AND FUELLING, humid and 25C+ at the start: carb-heavy lunch, light carb snack at 4pm, caffeine at 6pm at the exact dose you rehearsed on 9 Jan and not a milligram you have not tried. Pre-load fluid and electrolytes through the afternoon. Pre-cool before the warm-up: cold drink, wet towel on the neck, stay out of the sun. CHECKPOINTS have water, electrolyte and a small variety of food, but NO CUPS. Carry your own cup for anything you do not want in the bottle.  ||  WARM-UP CLOCK: 6:20pm start, 15 min easy, drills, 3 strides, done by 6:47pm. Keep it short and stay cool; in this humidity a long warm-up costs more than it gives.  ||  RACE THE CLOCK, NOT THE FIELD. THE TROPHY IS TOP THREE MALE. Three trophies for men, three for women, per race. No age-group awards, so your 30-39 placing is a progress gauge and nothing you can take home.  ||  VERIFIED from the official results, third MALE has been 56:09 (2024), 59:40 (2025) and 50:23 (2026). That is a nine and a half minute lottery you do not control. A time is yours. The 2026 male podium was 47:20, 48:49 and 50:23, and the top two were both 15-17 juniors, so the fast end of that range is the trend and not the outlier. Read it the other way and it is simple: sub-50 would have taken a trophy in every one of the last three years, comfortably in 2024 and 2025 and by 23 seconds in 2026. The time goal and the trophy are the same target. Sub-50 is therefore not the stretch above the podium. On a competitive year it is the entry fee.  ||  A goal: sub-50, run as the fastest time you can produce on the night. The placing takes care of itself or it does not, and either way it was never the thing you could train for.  ||  MANDATORY GEAR, straight off the Run Queensland event page, and this is not optional: mobile phone carrying the emergency numbers Brett Standring 0447 711 232 and Gavin Jackson 0417 007 960; race bib worn on the front and visible at all times; water bottle or hydration pack of at least 500ml; a compression bandage; headlight or suitable torch. Recommended on top: your own drinking cup, insect repellent, bite and sting treatment. Lay all of it out the night before and check it again at 6pm.  ||  ENTERED, both Daybreak and Night, confirmed 1 Sep 2026.
opt_out: Race day. 7:00pm, Mt Beerwah, 10.04km and 255m. Everything is rehearsed. Go and run it.
opt_tm: No.
hr_note: No ceiling and no pacing off the watch. Expect Z4 to Z5 (172-186) for most of it, above 187 on the 800m climb and again on the closing drag. Heart rate lags, it will read low on the climb when the effort is right and it will read high in the humidity when the effort is fine. Race the ground and the people, not the number. || ZONES (threshold HR 182, max 200): Z1 up to 153 | Z2 154-162 | Z3 163-171 | Z4 172-181 | Z5 182-186 | Z6+ 187 and up.
